author: Ewan Murray at Hampden Park
description:
A special occasion for Andy Robertson saw Scotland flirt with embarrassment. Collection of his 102nd cap moves Robertson level with Kenny Dalglish in the all-time Scottish list. By Monday night, Robertson will be a record holder. This was, however, John McGinn’s night. A double from McGinn, the second a penalty, spared Scottish blushes against a North Macedonia team who threatened to gatecrash Robertson’s celebration.

This proved an almighty struggle for Scotland. Questions – and plenty of them – surround whether or not Sébastien Pocognoli can build on the excellent work of his predecessor Steve Clarke. For now, Scotland are a tough watch. Pocognoli looks tactically inflexible and this is not the new dawn many predicted. Pocognoli must be careful not to deliver a lesson in being careful what you wish for.
title: John McGinn double saves Scotland’s blushes against North Macedonia

author: AFP
description:
Anti-corruption agency carried out searches as part of investigation into Orbán-era minister accused of taking bribes

Hungary’s anti-corruption agency said on Friday it had seized cash worth $19.5m (£14.8m) buried in forests and hidden elsewhere while investigating an ex-minister of nationalist former leader Viktor Orbán.

Miklós Seszták, Hungary’s minister of national development between 2014 and 2018, is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company, purchasing secondhand buses at inflated prices.

Continue reading...
title: Hungary seizes $19.5m in cash found buried in forests amid graft inquiry

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
• FC Andorra goalkeeper collided with De Miguel

  • Owono: ‘I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesús’

The FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesús de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week.

Owono, an Equatorial Guinea international, was sent off in the second division match on 2 November after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision, De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on 3 November.

Continue reading...
title: Jesús Owono given 12-match ban for tackle that resulted in Jesús de Miguel’s death

author: Agencies
description:
• Americans set tournament record with 85 shots on goal

  • Harvey and Winn score twice each in 14-0 rout

  • Canada edge Czechs 3-2 to set up Sweden semi-final

Defending champions the United States marched into the semi-finals of the women’s ice hockey world championship with a crushing 14-0 victory over hosts Denmark on Friday.

The Americans stormed out of the blocks, racing into a 5-0 lead inside eight minutes before stretching their advantage to 10-0 by the end of the second period in the first-ever meeting between the teams.

Continue reading...
title: USA hammer Denmark 14-0 with record 85 shots to reach women’s hockey worlds semi-finals

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Rescue efforts under way as American Heritage takes on water; governor confirms incident in Mississippi River

  • Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans

Pictures are now coming in from the news wires. Emergency personnel and crews can be seen on the scene after a tanker crashed into a river cruise in New Orleans. The cruise liner can be seen lying on its side:

Officials said they will be holding a news conference at 3pm CST, to begin in about ten minutes, providing further updates on the collision. We will bring you those latest updates as they come.

Continue reading...
title: New Orleans boat crash: tanker collides with river cruise ship carrying more than 130 people – latest updates

author: Guardian staff
description:
No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at Suffolk site affected, says US military

The US air force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an airbase in the east of England.

No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, the air force said.

Continue reading...
title: US air force responds to suspected drone activity at RAF Lakenheath

author: Dara Kerr
description:
US congresswoman, who has been caught up in repeated controversies, loses re-election bid to Democrat Eileen Laubacher

Lauren Boebert, the firebrand conservative Republican Colorado representative whose three terms in Congress have been marred by multiple controversies, was defeated in her re-election bid.

The gun rights advocate, born-again Christian and one-time QAnon fan lost to Democrat Eileen Laubacher by a less than 1% margin, according to the Associated Press.

Continue reading...
title: Trump-backed Maga firebrand Lauren Boebert defeated in Colorado congressional race

author: Auzzy Byrdsell in New York
description:
Authorities conclude search for victims in wreckage of the building and release the names of the eight victims

The New York City police department (NYPD) and New York City fire department (FDNY) have concluded the search for victims in the wreckage of the collapsed building in Brooklyn and released the names of the eight people who died.

A further 18 people were injured and one was still in critical condition Friday morning, after the disaster on a residential street on Wednesday that saw six men, a boy and a girl among those killed, amid demands for accountability.

Continue reading...
title: Officials name victims of fatal Brooklyn building collapse as investigation widens

author: Associated Press
description:
Trump officials seek to overturn lower court rulings that found executive order banning asylum applications illegal

The US supreme court agreed on Friday to consider Donald Trump’s ban on asylum at the US-Mexico border, a pillar of the Republican president’s far-reaching crackdown on immigration.

The Trump administration wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the executive order banning asylum applications is illegal.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court agrees to consider Trump’s ban on asylum at US-Mexico border

author: Jim Powell
description:
Russian airstrikes in Kyiv, floods in Gaza, Abdul El-Sayed in Washington and Cop31 – the past seven days as captured by the world’s leading photojournalists

Warning: this gallery contains images some readers may find distressing

Continue reading...
title: The week around the world in 20 pictures

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aisha Down ; produced by Hana Williams ; senior producer Angus Neale ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Jensen Huang’s resignation from the AI chipmaker Nvidia has sent shockwaves through the global economy. Huang resigned after reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The fallout is not over yet, with criticism mounting over the apparent lack of action from the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s global technology reporter, Aisha Down

Continue reading...
title: Why the Nvidia scandal is far from over - The Latest

author: Aisha Down Global technology reporter
description:
President purchased up to $5m of stock before revoking Biden-era rule that limited Nvidia’s ability to sell to China

Donald Trump bought Nvidia stock worth millions of dollars as he made decisions on America’s China policy that would benefit the chipmaker, an analysis has found.

In May 2025, Trump’s administration rescinded a Biden-era rule designed to prevent the most advanced US-made AI chips from being exported to China.

Continue reading...
title: Trump bought Nvidia stock as he helped chipmaker with change to export rule

author: Jenny Valentish
description:
The ‘first lady’ of Hobart’s Museum of Old and New Art has launched an OnlyFans portal with an ambitious – and controversial – goal

The forestry workers took unusual care as they picked their way through the mossy undergrowth of a Tasmanian forest. They were carrying a small group of furries – humans in animal suits that can cost thousands of dollars – mindful of not letting any tails drag in the mud. Hired as production crew for the day, they were more used to hearing the drone of heavy logging machinery than the moans of animal lust. Once the furries were in place, the director closed the set so that they could film their group sex scene in private.

“They were just adorable. Even when they’re doing adult acts, it still just looks really cute and kind of innocuous,” artist Kirsha Kaechele says.

Continue reading...
title: Can pornography help save Tasmania’s rainforests? Kirsha Kaechele hopes so

author: Editorial
description:
From Cairo to Moscow to Washington, governments are turning up the pressure on media workers

Lina Attalah is an influential Egyptian journalist. Yet until last month, even she was unaware of a major and concerning piece of news: her own conviction. In 2024, a court issued her a one-year sentence for “spreading false news” and running a website without a licence – which she had repeatedly sought to obtain – after trying her in absentia, even though she was in the country. Ms Attalah learned of the case only after she was separately tried in October, resulting in a large fine and an order for the closure of the Mada Masr website. She faces retrial later this month.

Meanwhile, the entire newsroom of the fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention weeks after authorities snatched the six journalis
title: The Guardian view on press freedom: authoritarians target journalism because it matters | Editorial

author: Editorial
description:
The End of Everything is a novel for our age of permacrisis. Genre boundaries belong to the past

“Science fiction will never be Literature with a capital ‘L,’” began a New York Times review of Margaret Atwood’s novel Oryx and Crake back in 2003. Now, the seemingly impossible has happened – M John Harrison’s The End of Everything is the first science fiction novel to win the Booker prize.

Fans have hailed this as a victory for a long-marginalised genre. The author himself was not so sure. “Writing science fiction is the last thing I want to do,” he said with characteristic iconoclasm at an event before the prize. The sci-fi v literary or “mainstream” fiction debate is as endless and battle-strewn as a fantasy saga. The late Urs
title: The Guardian view on M John Harrison’s Booker win: a new frontier for science fiction | Editorial

author: Gerard Meagher
description:
• ‘Japan have a distinct way of playing,’ says captain

  • Steve Borthwick hails ‘weird and wonderful’ Jones

Maro Itoje has insisted England will be ready for any curveballs Eddie Jones may throw on Saturday, warning his side they cannot “sleepwalk” into battle against Japan.

Jones, England’s longest-serving head coach after his stint between 2015 and 2022, has strongly hinted he will set his side up to unsettle his former charges at Twickenham, warning that they do not like “unorthodox” rugby. The hosts are heavy favourites to back up last week’s record win over Australia with another emphatic victory and have never lost to Japan but Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes, fielding an inexperienced side against that of his predecessor.
title: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into clash with Eddie Jones’s Japan

author: Gaby Hinsliff
description:
It is important to understand just how effectively perpetrators of abuse have used lawyers as their shields. A challenge to that can’t come soon enough

There will be empty shelves in many bedrooms this weekend, where the David Walliams books once stood. For parents of a certain era, there was no escaping that particular publishing-industrial complex, and I certainly did my share of wearily reading Gangsta Granny or Mr Stink on repeat. At his peak, Walliams was the bestselling children’s author in Britain for 100 weeks straight, to say nothing of the spin-off theatre productions, Christmas specials, countless World Book Day costumes, and that family-friendly stint as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent during which we now learn he was reportedly
title: Don’t just blame the culture for keeping powerful men’s dirty secrets. Blame the law too | Gaby Hinsliff

author: Joey Lynch at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium
description:
• Qatar 0-3 Australia (McGree 5, Yengi 32, Irankunda 40)

  • Julen Lopetegui under pressure as Qatar head coach

It was a win almost as comfortable as the buildup had been turbulent, as the Socceroos placed the drama of a week dominated by talk of everything but the football aside and cruised to a comprehensive 3-0 win over Qatar.

Pressing high, Australia’s men were ruthless in attack and dominant whenever their opponents even thought about getting forward, putting the result beyond doubt inside the opening 45 minutes. It took until the 38th for Qatar to register a touch in the Australia penalty area, and by that point they were down 2-0, with the third added for good measure just two minutes later. When Almoez Ali registered the reigning Asian champions’ first shot in the 72nd minute, Tony Popovic had emptied his bench, and the debutant Sam Klein hurled himself in front of the attempt before Patrick Beach had to worry about ma
title: McGree helps Socceroos put drama behind them and leave Qatar reeling

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Mohammed Alfatih rearrested over alleged plot to target Israelis in Europe while detained for attack on bailiff

A former Hamas bodyguard convicted of knife crime in the UK is wanted in Germany for allegedly plotting to murder Jewish people.

Details of the alleged plot can now be reported after Mohammed Alfatih, also known as Mohammed Naim, was found guilty on Friday of a knife attack on a bailiff outside his home in Birmingham.

Continue reading...
title: Former Hamas bodyguard convicted of Birmingham knife crime also wanted in Germany

author: Jonathan Freedland
description:
The environmental and economic dilemmas he faces are formidable but, with a bold plan, he could set an example for leaders around the world

For politicians of the centre-left especially, it’s the great dilemma of the age. How do you do what everyone can see is essential to save the planet from boiling – even as your voters demand action to get the economy growing and to make life more affordable? Plenty of activists will tell you there’s no contradiction, that tackling the climate crisis makes economic as well as ecological sense and, in the long term, you know they’re right. But you don’t live in the long term. You’re running the government right now and facing several unavoidable, binary choices.

Andy Burnham is a prime example. This week, he addressed the Cop summit in Antalya, promising “a new era of British leadership” in the struggle
title: Fight the climate crisis or go for growth? There is a way Burnham can do both | Jonathan Freedland

author: Carmen Rising
description:
Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams

On her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina. She works full-time as a gynecological teaching assistant (GTA) – a layperson who helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams before they work with actual patients.

It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. Contrary to common belief, pap smears – tests that screen for cervical cancer – don’t have to be painful.

Continue reading...
title: She gets 16 pap smears a day – so yours don’t hurt

author: Fiona Harvey, Oliver Milman and Graham Readfearn in Antalya
description:
António Guterres says climate action central to every aspect of UN’s work, as leaders depart Cop31 and talks go on

Tackling the climate crisis is central to all of human life and must be at the forefront of global governance, the outgoing UN secretary general has said in an emotional farewell address at the Cop31 climate summit.

“You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” António Guterres said at his final climate press conference as secretary general on Friday. “You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it. You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘You cannot build peace on a burning planet,’ UN chief tells Cop31 in farewell speech

author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
description:
Police say allegations of sexual misconduct are separate from those made by multiple women in Guardian and ITN investigation

The Metropolitan police have announced a criminal investigation into David Walliams over alleged sexual misconduct.

In reports by the Guardian and ITV News, Walliams, 55, has been accused by multiple women of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex.

Continue reading...
title: Met police launch investigation into David Walliams allegations

author: Guardian staff
description:
Late-night hosts poked fun at the president taking JD Vance off Iran duty to sniff out corruption while expressing annoyance at Democrats for failing to impeach Pete Hegseth

Late-night hosts ridiculed Donald Trump’s latest efforts to accuse Democrats of corruption while showing frustration over democratic behavior this week.

Continue reading...
title: Jimmy Kimmel on Trump accusing Democrats of wrongdoing: ‘His mantra is corruption’

author: Simon Burnton
description:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

So farewell then, Pierre Sage. Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate. The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] t
title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace

author: Aaron Bower
description:
Electrifying full-backs take centre stage in men’s final before Australia and New Zealand meet again in the women’s decider

In so many ways this has been a Rugby League World Cup of change. New formats, new stories, new nations rising and even the whisper of a rarity for this tournament: a financial profit. But for all the evolution and growth witnessed in the past month, the final acts arrive with a familiar international comfort blanket.

Perhaps the biggest surprise is that, while the men’s final in Brisbane is the one everyone expected, Australia and New Zealand are contesting it for the first time since 2013. In 2017, England tried and failed to dethrone the Kangaroos while four years ago it was Samoa who were beaten finalists. Now the Kiwis are next to try.
title: Ponga and Walsh lead old rivals into Rugby League World Cup showdown

author: Joe Plimmer
description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

Continue reading...
title: Maasai celebrations and Alpacas in a care home: photos of the day – Friday

author: Anna Isaac and Ben Quinn
description:
Exclusive: Sources reveal party is covering costs – raising new questions about leader’s explanation for billionaire’s gift

Nigel Farage’s personal security has been paid for out of Reform UK’s central funds despite his claim that these expenses would be covered by an undisclosed gift of £5m from a billionaire donor, sources have told the Guardian.

The Reform leader has had the central party pay for a team and two cars ever since a reduction in the security provided by the taxpayer after a review in 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Nigel Farage’s security paid for by Reform UK despite claim over £5m gift

author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
description:
Censored books spanning 1926-96 contained themes ‘likely to corrupt or deprave’, or references to contraception or violence

For almost a century, an Irish government building in the heart of Dublin has hosted a secret sanctum: the banned books room.

The department of justice, on St Stephen’s Green, did not grant public access, because the shelves contained 12,000 books deemed indecent or obscene.

Continue reading...
title: Banned books from Ireland’s room of ‘evil literature’ finally see the light of day

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
Once the ultimate symbol of Hollywood rebellion, the former Nvidia chief’s signature look is now being mocked as a midlife crisis cliche

For nearly two decades a black leather jacket has been a key part of Jensen Huang’s look. Now it has become a punchline.

As the founder and chief executive of Nvidia resigned this week after reports of multiple affairs, his affinity for a leather jacket, an item of clothing typically associated with a man in midlife crisis mode, has become widely mocked.

Continue reading...
title: Marlon Brando cool to Jensen Huang joke: how the black leather jacket became a meme

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Supplies outstripped demand by almost 2m barrels a day in October as market shows ‘tentative signs of rebalancing’

The world’s oil supply is swinging back to a surplus for the first time since the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran, the International Energy Agency (IEA) has said.

Oil supplies outstripped demand by almost 2m barrels a day in October, the Paris-based agency said, as “Gulf exports recovered much faster than global oil demand”.

Continue reading...
title: Global oil supply returns to surplus for first time since start of Iran war, says IEA

author: Presented by Madeleine Finlay with Ian Sample , produced by Joshan Chana, Luke John Smith and Jacob Liebenberg , graphics by Elliot Ellis and the executive producer was Ellie Bury
description:
Scientists at Dartmouth College in New Hampshire say they have discovered a telltale sign of an enjoyable conversation. Apparently the secret of a mutually satisfying chat is a healthy dose of pink noise. Guardian science editor Ian Sample tells co-host Madeleine Finlay how this concept usually associated with physics can be applied to conversation, and what the secret to pinkifying our chats could be.

Continue reading...
title: What science can tell us about the art of conversation - video

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Attack thought to be orchestrated by Kyiv comes day after Russian military official was killed in blast in St Petersburg

Russia has been rocked by two car bomb attacks that killed a senior military figure and seriously injured a suspected intelligence agent, in the latest in a series of assassination attempts believed to have been orchestrated by Kyiv.

On Friday morning a car bomb exploded in southern Moscow, severely injuring Sergei Zavorotniy, 72, a former senior aide to Ukraine’s exiled former prime minister Mykola Azarov.

Continue reading...
title: Moscow car bomb severely injures former aide to Ukraine’s pro-Russia ex-PM

author: Dmitrii Komarov
description:
A vodkatini-alike with a mellow shot of autumnal amber wine – serve cool with a spritz of lemon

Georgian wine brings gentle tannins and floral notes to a traditional martini base, giving the cocktail greater depth and complexity.

Dmitrii Komarov, bar manager, Sova, London W11

Continue reading...
title: Cocktail of the week: Sova’s amber martini – recipe | The good mixer

author: Lydia Wilkins
description:
His upcoming appearance on I’m a Celebrity, Get Me Out of Here! is already causing a huge stir. As he heads to Australia, the paralympian talks leeches, evil taxis – and snakes round his nether regions

‘If you spend enough time in the TV industry, at some point you’re going to end up in the jungle, eating animal genitalia, with Ant and Dec watching you!”

Paralympic medallist and TV presenter Ade Adepitan is in the building, and he’s ready to cause a stir. The 53-year-old is set to become the first wheelchair user on I’m a Celebrity, Get Me Out of Here!. His participation has already ignited a social media maelstrom, drawing ableist ire – from accusations of “cheating” due to the jungle being adapted for him to outright crowing that a disabled person should not be on a primetime show as it is ostensibly “box-ticking”.
title: ‘You can’t train to be chucked in a box full of rats!’ Ade Adepitan on fear, facing down sharks and being I’m a Celeb’s first wheelchair user

author: Samuel Woolley, Dean Jackson and Maia Woluchem
description:
Big tech has used misdirection, disinformation and jargon to obscure the harm the facilities can cause to communities

“Antifa”. “Commies”. “Chinese bots”. Everyone from tech leaders to the president has called datacenter resistance a “documented psyop” and a “Chinese PR thing”.

But why do they make these claims? Our new research finds that the datacenter industry uses propaganda, disinformation, and information control to mold public opinion and undermine community opposition.

Continue reading...
title: The datacenter industry is using propaganda to fight opposition | Samuel Woolley, Dean Jackson and Maia Woluchem

author: Miatta Mbriwa
description:
Ministers consider banning under-16s from online marketplaces amid reported misuse of messaging functions and users’ photos

In June, Hannah* listed her seven-year-old daughter’s pink swimming costume for sale on Vinted, hoping other parents surfing the reselling site would snap up the £1 offer. Her inbox pinged.

“So a little girl wore this yh [yeah]?” wrote a user with a male handle.

Continue reading...
title: The dark side of reselling apps: ‘If you include your pants, I’ll pay more’

author: Oliver Milman
description:
One company is proposing elongating the life of the dump, pungent smell and all, several more decades

As a visual representation of how New York is running out of places to put its waste, the largest active landfill in the state is a striking one. The hulking Seneca Meadows landfill is already the height of the Statue of Liberty and its operators are seeking to raise it even further, to the consternation of nearby residents.

The landfill, situated in the scenic Finger Lakes region in the northern reaches of New York state, has grown since the 1980s to now sprawl across 350 acres of deposited trash, mounded up to the height of around 300ft – roughly the same height of the Statue of Liberty.

Continue reading...
title: New York is running out of room for its waste even with Statue of Liberty sized landfill

author: Gabrielle Canon in Monterey Bay, California
description:
Water temperatures are climbing the charts, high tides are swallowing the shoreline and vital parts of the food web that feed ocean diversity are disappearing

On a picturesque autumn afternoon last week, the beaches of California’s Monterey Bay were teeming with life and death.

A cadre of shorebirds charged and retreated in a synchronized dance with the raging surf. Nearby, the receding tides had deposited lifeless bundles of feathers and bone, tangled in piles of glistening kelp. Swollen sea lion carcasses, their teeth bared in a quiet grimace, dotted the sand as beach picnickers and dog walkers enjoyed the warm, cloudless day.

Continue reading...
title: A super El Niño brings life and death to the California coast: ‘Like nothing we’ve ever seen’

author: Claire Finkelstein
description:
The failed move could lead to a more robust effort against the defense secretary in the next Congress. Here’s how it could look

A traffic jam, combined with disorganization on the part of Democrats, enabled House Republicans to scuttle the representative Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth on Wednesday.

While recriminations are now flying among Democrats, the fumble may have been a blessing in disguise. Democrats can now refocus the articles against the defense secretary, possibly to better effect.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats fumbled the Hegseth impeachment. That could be a blessing in disguise | Claire Finkelstein

author: Emily Maclean in Nairobi
description:
Effects of extreme weather expected in countries that already have high maternal and newborn death rates

El Niño stokes a higher risk of death in childbirth for millions of women in the world’s harshest crisis zones, midwives have warned.

Converging waves of weather – floods, cyclones and extreme heat – forecast to peak in the coming months will prove fatal for many, especially pregnant women, who face being cut off from hospital when in labour.

Continue reading...
title: El Niño will increase risk of death in childbirth for millions, say midwives

author: Sanya Mansoor
description:
The privacy issues over the company’s surveillance cameras have caused protests in schools all over the country

Angela Nguyen, a senior at Stanford University, has been on a mission to make sure her school doesn’t use automated license plate readers, like those made by Flock Safety, for mass surveillance. The 21-year-old computer science major helped collect hundreds of signatures earlier this year from students, faculty, alumni and residents to demand that Stanford drop its current Flock contract and codify safeguards for similar tech tools the school may use in the future. The fear, Nguyen says, is that these cameras, which show where a vehicle was at a certain point in time, can be exploited to victimize vulnerable people.

Stanford
title: US university students tell surveillance cameras to Flock off

author: Matthew Cantor
description:
Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse

Three days after a historic blue tsunami changed America’s political landscape, Elon Musk announced Tesla would end production of its hulking Cybertruck next year.

Was it a coincidence? Maybe. Musk said the move was “to make room for increased Cybercab production”, referring to Tesla’s Robotaxi. But the combined circumstances felt highly appropriate: it was the end of an era.

Continue reading...
title: Farewell, Cybertruck: why the winding down of the ‘Maga hat on wheels’ is a sign of the times

author: Dustin Guastella
description:
Progressives should be careful not to get comfortable. There is work to be done

Democrats had a great midterms result. Big wins in Ohio, Georgia, Iowa, Maine and Texas show the potential for a majority coalition that reaches well beyond traditional liberal strongholds. That’s a good sign for the party’s chances come 2028.

Not surprisingly, the story of the midterms was “affordability”. Surveys showed that the economy was the top issue for the election, with a third of voters citing cost-of-living concerns as their number one issue, and nearly 40% of voters claiming their personal financial situation has worsened over the past year. It’s clear that voters don’t approve of Donald Trump’s economic management.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats need to fix these three weaknesses before 2028 | Dustin Guastella

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
Debate over climate science, transition away from fossil fuels, electrification and climate finance can begin in earnest as world leaders leave UN summit

Given Sheldon Whitehouse’s often lonely climate advocacy in American politics, it is grimly suitable that he is the only US senator here at Cop31.

The Rhode Island lawmaker is with a group of other Democrats who are, in a sort of unofficial way, representing the US. Donald Trump has, for the second year in a row, not sent a delegation to Cop and has recently spent time talking about solar panels frying animals to death and how he won’t allow any “loser” wind turbines.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31 live: Climate crisis negotiations heat up on fifth day of talks

author: Stephen Collins
description: Continue reading...
title: I’m a turtle, get me out of here! The Stephen Collins cartoon

author: Ali Martin at Optus Stadium, Perth
description:
A week of quietly watching Australian cricket descend into civil war ended with smiles being wiped from English faces as a stunning debut from fast bowler Mahli Beardman consigned the tourists to an all-too-familiar hammering in Perth.

Victory in a low-key one-day international was never going to atone for the galling start to that failed Ashes campaign here 12 months ago. Nevertheless, England appeared better prepared, while their hosts were missing their big three fast bowlers and fighting sandpaper-related bushfires off the field.

Continue reading...
title: Australia race to paltry target after debutant quick Beardman routs England in first ODI

author: Lanre Bakare
description:
After wittily blending pop and politics on their debut, the Belgians are now processing their personal lives. We join them for a mindbending tour of their home city of Ghent

Boris Kor Tom Zeebroek is staring up at a grey gothic building in the centre of Ghent, squinting through the late September sun that is covering his home town in a cloak of unseasonal warmth.

Zeebroek is encouraging his bandmate Charlotte Adigéry and I to crane our necks towards the Mammelokker, an 18th-century Flemish relief on the top of the building. It’s a gruesome bit of stone, which sits above the town square and depicts a daughter suckling her own father. The pair are taking me on a tour of their medieval home town, and this disturbing architectural decoration is part of our itinerary.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Would you breastfeed your own father?’ The goofy, spiky world of art-pop duo Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul

author: Oliver Milman in Antalya
description:
In this week’s newsletter: The climate summit has a new floor-filler to ‘bring down the heat’, but it may struggle to get countries to sing a different environmental tune

• Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The UN’s annual climate summit is known for being arcane, long-winded and frustrating. On Wednesday, however, Turkey brought a dash of Eurovision-style glamour to proceedings.

The hosts of the talks, held in the historic Mediterranean city of Antalya, decided to blast assorted world leaders, dignitaries and other delegates with Let’s Cop, a bona fide floor-filler that includes the lines: “Bring down the heat, make it drop. One world, one call, let’s Cop.”
title: A new song gives Cop31 Eurovision vibes – but how should we score progress so far?

author: Sam Leith
description:
The US reporter wrongly imprisoned for espionage writes compellingly about his ordeal

Evan Gershkovich is the Wall Street Journal reporter who, in the early phase of Putin’s war in Ukraine, was snatched up by the Russian authorities on bogus espionage charges and spent a year and a half in Russian jails (first Lefortovo and then Yekaterinburg) before being released in a prisoner exchange in 2024.

The opening section of his book about the experience is gripping and rather moving. He recounts his arrest in a sting operation, after meeting a contact who promised to supply him with information about Russia’s military-industrial preparations. Born to Russian Jewish immigrant parents in the US, Gershkovich grew up in suburban New Jersey on a diet of Soviet cartoons and “Krylov’s fables rather than Aesop’s”; he was betwixt and between. When he found his way into journalism in his early 20s – first working nights as an editorial assistant at th
title: This Cursed Beautiful Land by Evan Gershkovich review – jailed in Putin’s Russia

author: Andrew Beasley
description:
Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team

Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League fina
title: Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
Men are routinely getting more wool for their money – are women really paying a pink tax when they buy a jumper?

• Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s officially cosy season. But before you treat yourself to a new wooly jumper, you may want to take a closer look at the care label.

Abercrombie & Fitch is facing a pink tax backlash, sparked by a video on TikTok that highlights the difference between the materials used in menswear and womenswear jumpers that cost the same.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Pretty weird’: How a viral video shows a striking discrepancy in men and women’s knitwear

author: Guardian readers
description:
From the Isle of Skye to the Cairngorms, our explorers find white-sand beaches, secret lochs and solitude

• Tell us about your favourite European national park – the best tip wins a £200 holiday voucher

At Camasunary bay on the Strathaird peninsula of the Isle of Skye, we watched an otter at low tide lifting seaweed to find crabs. Boots off, we crossed one of Skye’s shortest (and coldest) rivers, before slogging upwards through unforgiving heather to the col beneath the pathless hill Sgùrr na Strì. The mountain view from the summit’s glaciated slabs is perhaps the finest in Scotland – or even Europe. Below is landlocked Loch Coruisk, girdled by the black teeth of the entire Cuillin ridge. Extraordinary. An hour passed, maybe two, before we head
title: ‘I found the best mountain view in Europe’: readers’ favourite wild escapes in Scotland

author: Phil Harrison, Jack Seale, Graeme Virtue and Simon Wardell
description:
John Sparks looks at the shocking links with the cocaine market. Plus, Sarah Cox, Mel Giedroyc and more host this year’s Children in Need. Here’s what to watch this evening

9pm, Sky Documentaries

Continue reading...
title: TV tonight: an absorbing investigation about the Albanian mafia

author: Gary Fuller
description:
Research finds highest levels of cancer-related PAH pollutants in cities that have widespread wood heating

Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust, suggests new research across six European towns and cities.

Scientists measured the air in buildings where children spend much of their time; in schools, sports centres and homes. Specifically, they looked at polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), a family of pollutants that are given off when fuels are burned.
title: Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as traffic exhaust, study suggests

author: Andy Beckett
description:
From the US midterms to Brazil and Hungary, extremists are floundering yet the left still overestimates their power. Reality is on our side

From Brazil to Hungary and Britain to the US, why are so many people so surprised by the right’s election defeats? Flávio Bolsonaro, Viktor Orbán, Reform UK, the Tories and a vast array of Republican candidates have all been rejected in national or local contests this year, even in usually reliably conservative Mississippi. Apparently impregnable incumbents and populist insurgents alike have been beaten, often by big margins. The supposedly ascendant global right has been out-organised, out-thought, outmanoeuvred and outnumbered.

Yet each time this happens – which is more often than the usual gloomy narrative of our politics allows – many libe
title: Progressives are still so pessimistic, but why? The populist right can and will be defeated | Andy Beckett

author: Melanie Wilkinson
description:
Pairing these statement pieces can be tricky. For a surprisingly easy twist, try contrasting fabrics – a denim shirt, a cosy knit – alongside pared-back accessories

Continue reading...
title: What to wear with a leather skirt

author: Sarah Johnson
description:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.
title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Bournemouth became a hub for thousands of finance jobs after the 1980s big bang, but new tech risks hurting Dorset’s economy

A few minutes’ drive from Bournemouth’s sandy beachfront, on the site of a former farm, lies an unlikely nerve centre of international finance.

Here, miles from the glass towers of London’s Canary Wharf, more than 5,300 staff including compliance officers, analysts and software engineers help process more than $1tn (£750bn) worth of global transactions each day for the largest US bank, JP Morgan.

Continue reading...
title: ‘They’ve cut all entry-level jobs’: unlikely seaside town on frontline of AI threat

author: Alexis Petridis
description:
The band’s uneven 2003 album has been judiciously reworked to accompany a staging of Shakespeare’s tragedy with quite extraordinary results

According to the programme notes, Thom Yorke had serious reservations about director Christine Jones’ idea to stage a production of Hamlet featuring music from Radiohead’s 2003 album Hail to the Thief. Who can blame him? Many criticisms have been laid at Radiohead’s door but being hopelessly naff isn’t one of them, and, alas, naff is very much the adjective you’d apply to a lot of attempts to meld Shakespeare and rock music.

You’re often in the realm of high camp – portentous, Bard-quoting heavy metal lyrics; Return to the Forbidden Planet’s jokey blending of The Tempest with 50s rock’n’roll; 2015’s
title: Hamlet Hail to the Thief could have been rotten but redeems Radiohead’s ‘record that got away’ | Alexis Petridis

author: Helen Goh
description:
Cold pears stained red with tart hibiscus and offset by a hot, creamy, spiced rice pudding

Hibiscus has a tart, berry-like flavour, and turns these pears a jewel-bright crimson in colour. The pears are best poached a day ahead, because they’ll deepen in colour and flavour while they chill in the syrup. I especially like the contrast of the cold, gently tangy pears against a warm, creamy rice pudding that’s fragrant with cardamom, bay, lemon and vanilla. A scattering of pistachios adds a final touch of both colour and crunch.

Continue reading...
title: Helen Goh’s recipe for rice pudding with hibiscus-poached pears | The sweet spot

author: Lucy Mangan
description:
From the moment a contortionist crawls out of a bank vault, the 12-hour hunt for the culprits is a thrilling ride. Just suspend your disbelief a bit and strap in for a fantastic time

A contortionist crawls out of a safety deposit box in the wall of an underground Swiss bank vault, legs wrapped around his waist, feet resting on his lumbar spine, landing on hands and displaced knees on the tiled floor. You know what? SOLD. You have just earned my undivided attention for the next hour of whatever you want to present to me.

Under such highly promising circumstances does the new heist thriller 12 12 12 begin. It stars Anthony Mackie of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and Jamie Dornan (building a nice career since 2013’s The Fall, if we gloss over the 50 Shades movies and the one where he played a romantic hero
title: 12 12 12 review – Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s super fun heist hunt

author: Samuel McKee
description:
A mother hippopotamus protecting her young is one of the most fearsome forces of nature. Luckily, I’d just married someone ready to meet it head-on

Anna and I got married in Portugal in September last year. We had been together for 13 years. She said in her vows, “I don’t know what life is going to have in store for us, but I know our love for each other is always constant.”

Ten days later, I found myself in a swamp in Botswana with my intestines hanging out of my back.

Continue reading...
title: Experience: I was disembowelled by a hippo on my honeymoon

author: Written by Snigdha Poonam and read by Maya Saroya. Produced by Nicola Alexandrou. The executive producer was Ellie Bury
description:
Writers are being bombarded daily with invitations from fake book groups and offers to publicise their work. For the scamming industry, aspiring authors can be a soft touch

By Snigdha Poonam. Read by Maya Saroya

title: Fake film deals and emails from top agents: who is behind the explosion in literary scams? – podcast

author: Ana Naomi de Sousa
description:
While Spain, Germany and the UK have all introduced laws protecting renters’ rights, Luís Montenegro’s centre-right government is empowering landlords

As Storm Charles reached Portugal’s shores this week, flights were aborted, schools were closed, and the global Web Summit in Lisbon was forced to cancel a whole day of lucrative events. But even the promise of some very bad weather was not enough to deter housing protesters from setting up camp for another night on the streets.

Since 14 October, echoing recent eruptions over housing in Spain, and the fierce student-led protests in France, Lisbon and Porto have become the focus for encampments and daily protests drawing people in their thousands. Almost one month later, they show no sign of disappearing.
title: As housing protests sweep Portugal, police and politicians here seem bent on making the crisis worse | Ana Naomi de Sousa

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya
description:
Exclusive: Fossil fuels no longer dominant energy source, IEA leader says, as summit considers electrification pledge

The world has left behind the age of coal, oil and gas and is now firmly in “the age of electricity”, the world’s leading energy economist has said.

Fatih Birol, the executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said more than twice as much electricity generation would be added to the global economy in the next decade than in the last, as countries scramble to secure their energy supplies against fossil fuel price volatility and supply shocks, such as the Iran war.

Continue reading...
title: World is now in ‘age of electricity’, energy agency chief says at Cop31

author: Leah Harper
description:
Property sales that complete on this day have a lower median price. Air fares are cheaper. Weddings are non-existent. And motor collisions increase. How did it become so mired in superstition?

“I have only worked one Friday 13th wedding in my 14 years in business,” says Caroline Smyth, a photographer and celebrant based in Larne, Northern Ireland. “I definitely think it is down to the fact that it’s a date surrounded by superstition. People are maybe afraid it’s a bad omen for their marriage.”

Smyth’s sole Friday 13th wedding, in September 2013, was the first she ever photographed – and it kickstarted her career. But for many businesses, the date is not so auspicious. From weddings to flights, job interviews to elective surgeries, many people avoid booking anything of significance on this date, believing it to be bad luck.

Continue rea
title: The sinister power of Friday 13th: how this maligned date affects our lives

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
Backed by MPs from across the political divide, Bavarian Ilse Aigner offers an approachability and warmth the chancellor lacks

Germany has had 12 presidents since the end of the second world war, all of them men. Now, for the first time, the federal republic is on the brink of getting a female head of state. But Ilse Aigner, the lead candidate for the post, is unusual in more ways than one.

“No law degree. No marriage. No penis,” is how the left-leaning Taz newspaper put it this week – a wry, if blunt, assessment of what a break with history the 61-year-old Bavarian represents.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The time is ripe’: ex-helicopter engineer poised to be Germany’s first female president

author: Ryan Gilbey
description:
The teen pop star turned Olivier-winning actor stars as Andrew Scott’s best friend in the acclaimed Ian Charleson biopic. She talks kindred spirits, social media and trying to channel a ‘mad storm of grief’

The late Billie Whitelaw, whom Samuel Beckett considered “a perfect actress”, was on stage in the middle of rehearsals one day when she asked the playwright: “Where should I be looking?” To which Beckett replied: “Inwards.”

Hearing this story, another Billie – the teen pop star turned Doctor Who companion and Olivier award-winning powerhouse Billie Piper – lets out a laugh so raucous and expansive, it is as if a flock of gaily coloured birds has been released into the room, flapping and squawking in every corner. “Fuck, that’s awesome,” she says.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Women are pitted against each other. It’s a blood sport’: Billie Piper on industry infighting, Elsinore’s Oscar buzz and thriving on personal crisis

author: Emma Joyce and agencies
description:
Used in the famous ‘I am your father’ scene, the on-screen prop was originally expected to sell for a fraction of the price

Auctioneers estimated it would sell for over $1m, but on Thursday a Star Wars lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the famous “I am your father” scene from The Empire Strikes Back ended up selling for nearly $5m.

Darth Vader’s saber was one of 27 lightsaber props up for sale by Heritage Auctions in the US, including ones used by Ewan McGregor’s Obi-Wan Kenobi and Hayden Christensen’s Anakin Skywalker in Revenge of the Sith.

Continue reading...
title: Darth Vader’s lightsaber, used in Star Wars movies The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, sells for nearly $5m

description:
• Updates from the ODI series opener at Perth Stadium

  • Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email

All the talk of past deeds and perhaps even future global tournaments can be pushed aside as Xavier Bartlett stands at the top of his mark with Tom Banton on strike and Ben Duckett at the other end. Let’s play …

Thanks for Will to nudging attention closer to the action in Perth as the players line up for the Welcome to Country and the national anthems.

Continue reading...
title: Australia v England: first men’s cricket one-day international – live

author: Jonathan Watts
description:
Country’s fiercest blazes in at least a decade produced toxic smog blamed for 400,000 respiratory infections

Indonesia’s fiercest fires in at least a decade were amplified by an “El Niño that turned off the taps” and “fossil fuels that turned up the heat”, scientists have revealed.

Along with the conversion of forests to plantations, this created the conditions for blazes that have burned almost 3m hectares (7.4m acres) – 19 times the size of Greater London – this year, and cast a choking haze across much of south-east Asia.

Continue reading...
title: ‘El Niño turned off the taps’: factors behind Indonesia’s wildfires revealed

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
William, 17, says ‘nights were pretty cold’ and he ‘honestly didn’t think’ he’d survive

A teenage boy who survived almost a week lost in dense Australian bushland sang John Denver’s Take Me Home, Country Roads as he held out hope of rescue on long nights alone in the wilderness.

William, whose surname has been withheld, was dropped off by his mother for the weekend to camp with his friend in Victoria’s east last Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Chips, creek water and Take Me Home, Country Roads: how an Australian teenager survived six nights in the bush

author: Guardian sport
description:
Australian cricket captain breaks silence over allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about 2018 ball tampering in South Africa

After a torrid week, Australia’s Test captain, Pat Cummins, promised he would answer every question thrown at him in one of the most eagerly anticipated press conferences in recent sporting memory.

And, over the course of 70 minutes at Cricket Central in Sydney, he did just that, covering a range of topics from sandpaper and ball tampering to Australian cricket culture and his friendship with Usman Khawaja, whose book Sabr, released on Tuesday, has caused ructions in the Australian cricket community.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Abrasive’, ‘arrogant’ and ‘ugly’: standout moments from Pat Cummins’ sandpapergate press conference

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Hidden bunker, entered via a hatch in a field, controlled a gun battery used to attack German ships in Channel

It has been kept secret for decades, buried four metres deep into the white cliffs of Dover. But from Friday, members of the public will finally be able to visit a pioneering command bunker that was ordered by Winston Churchill and proved a vital defence during the second world war.

The Fan Bay plotting room, which is encased in concrete, housed the first land-based computer-aided targeting system. This acted as a “brain” for a gun battery that was used to defend Dover and attack German ships in the Channel, according to Jon Stewart, who led the excavation project for the National Trust.

Continue reading...
title: Second world war ‘brain’ bunker in cliffs of Dover opens to public
